questions.note: Order is right: the hallux leads, toe 2 sits well behind, and the hallux now ends in a blunt, domed pulp. Individual shaping is weak: stamped parallel wrinkles at the hallux IP and toe 2 PIP, a knife-cut DIP crease, toe 2 an even tube, a cuff step under toe 2, boxy plantar pads with a cap rim, no base crease under the hallux. Toes 3–5 declared, not judged.

Plates have thickness and folds, neither float nor sink, the corner tears are gone and toe 2's distal groove is soft. Both read as acrylic press-ons: opaque milky French-tip free edges, bold brushed streaks, an even gutter-and-rim pocket, no hallux lunula, a frosted plate. By eye in hr.front (21.7 px/mm) the hallux plate spans ~20.5 mm (19.5 target), toe 2's ~11.

Barely there. In hr.front no EHL cord rises over the first MTP or the hallux's proximal phalanx, no extensor slip runs toward toe 2, and the distal dorsum has no veins; hr.medial's dorsal contour is smooth. The one raised line, across the first MTP, reads as a scar. V1 and the saphenous vein are not in this packet, so judged from hr.front and hr.medial.

SSS is believable: toe shadow sides stay darker and warm, no glow. Micro-relief is wrong in kind: a uniform, dark-outlined Voronoi crackle ~0.45–0.75 mm on the toes (spec 0.25–0.4), crazed porcelain at native size; no follicle pits; pad ridges are straight corduroy at one angle, no whorls. The dorsum has a broad wet sheen. Colour is the declared first pass.

defects.what: Both nail plates are combed with bold, crisp white longitudinal streaks wherever a highlight falls, like brushed metal: across toe 2's whole plate here and over the hallux plate's distal half.
defects.fix: Real ridging is faint and irregular (0.25 mm pitch, about 0.01 mm deep): a soft ripple at the edge of a highlight, broken and uneven, never a fine comb of bright lines.

defects.what: The hallux free edge, and toe 2's, is an even, opaque milk-white rolled bead of constant width with a wavy contour, ridges striping its cut face: a French-manicure tip, not a trimmed toenail.
defects.fix: A trimmed toenail ends nearly straight with slightly rounded corners: a thin, translucent ivory edge of uneven width, layered on its cut face, with a narrow onychodermal band and a faint grime line beneath.

defects.what: No lunula: the hallux plate is one frosted grey-pink from fold to free edge, with no pale crescent at the root and no pink bed reading through a clear plate.
defects.fix: Show a pale 3.5 mm lunula crescent emerging from the proximal fold, and a clear plate over a pink bed that pales only toward the free edge.

defects.what: Each plate sits in an even rounded-rectangle pocket: a continuous gutter and piped rim run round the hallux and toe 2 plates, a second ridge echoes the proximal fold, and the plate's root shows a glossy white lip; the nail reads as an inset panel.
defects.fix: Lateral folds roll over the plate's sides and hide its edges; the proximal fold and cuticle lie flat on the plate with no gutter, and the outline is soft and slightly asymmetric.

defects.what: The hallux IP dorsal wrinkles are three identical, evenly spaced, parallel arcs of equal depth with glossy lips, one sculpted stroke repeated; edge-on in hr.medial they corrugate the contour.
defects.fix: Knuckle skin carries a loose cluster of fine, unequal wrinkles that branch, cross, fade at their ends and vary in depth and spacing, deepest over the joint line.

defects.what: Toe 2's PIP knuckle carries four or five evenly spaced, concentric grooves of equal length and depth, a bellows stamp rather than knuckle skin.
defects.fix: A PIP knuckle shows a few short, irregular transverse wrinkles, uneven in length and depth, often over a slightly thickened, pinker patch from boot pressure.

defects.what: Toe 2's dorsal DIP crease is one long, even groove with a bright lip running almost the full width of the toe, which reads as a knife cut.
defects.fix: A DIP shows two or three short, soft, shallow creases that fade toward the sides of the toe.

defects.what: A thin, raised, glossy line arcs across the first MTP dorsum at the hallux base; edge-on in hr.medial it makes a row of bumps. It reads as a healed incision scar, not a skin crease.
defects.fix: Over the first MTP the skin is smooth or carries a few short, soft transverse wrinkles that deepen only when the toe extends; no raised line.

defects.what: A crisp straight step rings toe 2's plantar middle phalanx, smooth skin above and ridged skin below, so the tip reads as a thimble or glove finger glued on (toes 3 and 4 show the same seam).
defects.fix: Plantar skin is continuous: flexion creases are soft curved folds at the joints, and friction ridges fade in gradually with no step in the surface.

defects.what: From below the hallux and toe 2 pads are rounded boxes with straight, parallel sides; the hallux distal pad is bounded by a raised rim at the IP crease, so it sits on the toe like a cap.
defects.fix: Real pulps are oval, fleshy domes, widest mid-pad and bulging past the toe's sides, blending into the proximal pad through a soft crease.

defects.what: No digito-plantar crease at the hallux base: from below the toe grows straight out of the ball, and only the IP crease marks it.
defects.fix: A sole shows a deep, curved fold where the hallux pad meets the ball, running from the 1–2 web across the toe's base.

defects.what: Skin relief is a uniform Voronoi crackle: closed, dark-outlined polygons about 0.45–0.75 mm across on the toes (spec 0.25–0.4), equally deep everywhere and unchanged over creases and nail folds; crazed porcelain at native size.
defects.fix: Toe skin shows fine, shallow, open furrows with a preferred direction, aligning with creases and the nail folds, plus follicle pits; at this scale it is barely visible.

defects.what: Friction ridges are straight parallel stripes at one diagonal angle over the sole, the hallux pad and toe 2's pad, continuing through the flexion creases like corduroy; no whorl or loop on either pulp.
defects.fix: Toe pulps carry whorls or loops centred on the pad; ridges curve round the tip, break at each flexion crease and change direction between segments.

defects.what: In profile the hallux's plantar IP crease is a sharp V-notch whose distal side overhangs as a hard lip, with an S-fold climbing the medial side, as if the toe were two tubes jointed.
defects.fix: The IP flexion crease is a soft, shallow notch; the proximal phalanx's fleshy plantar pad curves gently down into the bulging pulp.

defects.what: The 1–2 web's free margin is a straight oblique edge from the hallux's wall to toe 2's, a flat shelf between the toes; in hr.front it is a level line across the top of the gap.
defects.fix: A 1–2 web is a soft U-shaped saddle whose deepest point is set back between the toes, its margin climbing each toe's side.

defects.what: Toe 2 is an even-width tube from the PIP knuckle to the pulp: parallel sides, no waist over the middle phalanx, no DIP swelling; only the curl gives it a hump.
defects.fix: A second toe widens at the PIP knuckle, narrows over the short middle phalanx, swells slightly at the DIP and flares into a bulbous pulp.

defects.what: No extensor relief in frame: no EHL cord over the first MTP or along the hallux's proximal phalanx, no extensor slip toward toe 2, and no dorsal veins on the distal forefoot.
defects.fix: On a lean 40-year-old the EHL stands as a 0.5–1.5 mm cord to the hallux catching the rim light, with a fainter slip to toe 2 and low veins on the distal dorsum.

defects.what: A short, sharp, dark slit runs down from the hallux nail's medial distal corner into the pulp (a smaller one at the lateral corner), like a cut.
defects.fix: The lateral nail groove fades out softly into the distal groove at each corner.

defects.what: A tiny bright fleck sits under the hallux free edge in clay, at the hyponychium, as if the plate's underside pokes through the skin.
defects.fix: The hyponychium meets the plate's underside cleanly, with a small shadowed subungual gap under the free edge.

ranked: [D2] The nails give it away first: the hallux and toe 2 free edges are even, opaque, milk-white rolled beads of constant width, a French manicure. A trimmed toenail ends in a thin, translucent ivory edge of uneven width, cut nearly straight.
[D1] Every nail highlight is combed into bold white longitudinal streaks, like brushed metal; real ridging shows only as a faint, broken ripple at the edge of a highlight.

[D4] Each plate sits in an even rounded-rectangle pocket, gutter and piped rim all round plus a second ridge behind the proximal fold and a glossy white lip at the root: an inset panel. Real folds roll over the plate and hide its edges.

[D12] All the skin is a uniform, dark-outlined Voronoi crackle at nearly twice the spec's cell size, crazed porcelain at native size; real toe skin shows faint, directional furrows that follow creases and nail folds.
[D9] Under toe 2 a crisp straight step rings the middle phalanx, smooth above and ridged below, a thimble glued on; no real toe has a seam there.
[D10] From below the hallux and toe 2 pads are rounded boxes with straight sides, the hallux pulp capped by a raised rim at its IP crease; real pulps are oval domes, widest mid-pad.
[D16] Toe 2 is an even tube from knuckle to pulp, with no waist over the middle phalanx and no DIP swelling; only its curl gives it shape.
[D5] The hallux IP wrinkles are three identical, evenly spaced parallel arcs with glossy lips; knuckle skin has a loose, uneven cluster of fine wrinkles.
[D6] Toe 2's PIP carries four or five evenly spaced concentric grooves, a bellows stamp rather than knuckle skin.
[D7] Toe 2's DIP crease is one long, even, bright-lipped groove across the toe, a knife cut, where a real DIP shows two or three short soft creases.
[D8] A thin, raised, glossy line arcs across the first MTP at the hallux's base and reads as a healed bunionectomy scar.
[D13] Plantar friction ridges run as straight stripes at one angle over sole and pulps and through the creases, corduroy; the pulps have no whorls or loops.
[D3] No lunula on the hallux and little pink bed under the plate, so the nail reads frosted rather than a clear plate on living tissue.
[D11] From below the hallux grows straight out of the ball with no base crease where its pad meets the ball.
[D15] The 1–2 web's margin is a straight shelf between the toes, level across the gap in hr.front, instead of a U-shaped saddle set back between them.
[D14] In profile the hallux's plantar IP crease is a sharp V-notch with a hard overhanging lip and an S-fold up the medial side, as if the toe were jointed tubes.
[D17] No EHL cord, no extensor slip to toe 2 and no veins anywhere in frame; on a lean man the forefoot would not be this featureless.
[D18] Sharp little slits run from the hallux nail's distal corners into the pulp, like cuts.
The toes are bald: no tuft on the hallux's proximal phalanx and none on toe 2, so they read younger and more mannequin-like than the anchor feet (hair is outside this round's questions).

By eye: in hr.medial (17.9 px/mm) the hallux is ~21 mm deep at the IP and ~18.5 at the nail root, inside the table but short of the direction's ~25; the 1–2 gap is ~2–2.5 mm at the pulps in hr.plantar and hr.toe2, about half the 4.5 mm direction.
[D19] A tiny bright fleck under the hallux free edge in clay suggests the plate's underside pokes through the hyponychium.
